# How to Book KTX Train Tickets in Korea as a Foreigner

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/how-to-book-ktx-korea/
Last checked: 2026-10-23

## Quick answer

- Book in English on Korail's official site for foreigners (korail.com/global/eng) or in the KORAIL+ app. The normal booking window opens at 07:00 (Korea time) two months before your travel date; Seollal and Chuseok holiday trains follow a separate schedule.
- KTX and SRT merged on September 1, 2026. The government says they now run as KTX, with fares on average 10% lower than before. Seoul–Busan (via Gyeongju) is ₩54,400 in standard class.
- Keep your email and password — that's how you look up a ticket booked on the foreigner site, and you'll need them to cancel online before departure.

![A blue KTX-Cheongryong high-speed train waiting at a platform at Seoul Station](/img/photo-ktx-seoul-station.jpg?v=326e9396 "A KTX-Cheongryong train at Seoul Station, 2024. Photo: 생각하는 나무 (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

The KTX is Korea's high-speed train, and you can book it in English before you arrive. There's one change you won't find in older guides: on September 1, 2026, the KTX and the SRT — the high-speed trains that used to run from Suseo Station under a separate company — started running as one service called KTX. So if a blog post sends you to a separate SRT website, it's out of date.

## The short version

| | What to know |
|---|---|
| Where to book | Korail's site for foreigners (korail.com/global/eng), the KORAIL+ app, ticket machines or station counters — not at subway stations |
| When tickets go on sale | Normally from 07:00 (Korea time), two months before your travel date — holiday trains differ |
| How to pay | Credit card (online) |
| Finding your ticket | The email address and password you used when booking |
| Cancelling | Online before departure; after departure, generally at a station counter (see the KORAIL+ exception below) |

Source: [Korail — ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets) and [purchase and refund guide](https://www.korail.com/ticket/reserve/guide/pay) (Korean); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## What changed in September 2026

Korea used to have two high-speed operators: Korail ran the KTX, and a separate company, SR, ran the SRT from Suseo Station. After the companies were merged, the government says the two started running as KTX from September 1, 2026. Three things matter for visitors:

- **One place to book.** Integrated trains are booked through the KORAIL+ app and the Korail website. KORAIL+ replaced Korail's old app, Korail Talk.
- **Lower fares.** The government says KTX fares were brought down to former SRT levels — about 10% lower on average.
- **More seats on trains from Suseo.** Most of the added trains run on the Suseo routes, which the government says have about 30% more seats.

Source: [Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Aug 31, 2026](https://www.korea.kr/news/policyNewsView.do?newsId=148970889) and [Aug 3, 2026](https://www.korea.kr/news/policyNewsView.do?newsId=148969267) (Korean); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## How much a KTX ticket costs

These are adult standard-class fares from Korail's official KTX fare table, effective September 1, 2026:

| Route | Standard class |
|---|---|
| Seoul – Busan (via Gyeongju) | ₩54,400 |
| Suseo – Busan | ₩52,900 |
| Seoul – Dongdaegu (Daegu) | ₩39,000 |
| Seoul – Gyeongju | ₩44,500 |
| Seoul – Daejeon | ₩21,600 |
| Yongsan – Gwangju Songjeong | ₩42,000 |
| Yongsan – Jeonju | ₩31,600 |
| Yongsan – Yeosu EXPO | ₩45,400 |

Fares vary by route — the same two cities can have different fares depending on the stops a train makes — so check the price shown when you book. Korail's table also notes that the 10% reduction was set for three years and may be adjusted later.

![Rows of grey standard-class seats inside a KTX-Cheongryong carriage](/img/photo-ktx-standard-class.jpg?v=b1b9743d "Standard class on a KTX-Cheongryong train, 2024. Photo: 생각하는 나무 (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

Source: [Korail — KTX fare table, as of Sep 1, 2026](https://www.korail.com/ticket/reserve/train-timeTable) (Korean, Excel download); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Booking online, in English

![Booking a KTX ticket in four steps: open Korail's English site or the KORAIL+ app, search, save your email and password, pay by credit card](/img/ktx-steps.png?v=a7f9ef86 "Booking in four steps. Details below.")

1. Go to **korail.com/global/eng** — Korail's official site for foreigners. (The old letskorail.com address now redirects to korail.com.)
2. Search your departure station, arrival station, date and number of passengers, and pick a train.
3. Enter an email address and a password. Korail says you need to type them exactly — including upper- and lower-case letters — to look up your ticket later, and suggests writing them down.
4. Pay by credit card.
5. To check or cancel, open **MY TICKET** and enter the same email and password.

Source: [Korail — official site for foreigners](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/main) and [ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Save the email and password in your phone's notes the moment you book. Without them you can't pull up the ticket on the foreigner site.

## When tickets go on sale

Korail says the normal booking window opens at **07:00 (Korea time), two months before** the departure date. Online, you can buy until the train leaves; ticket machines stop selling 10 minutes before departure, and station counters sell until departure.

The big exception is Korea's two main holidays. Seollal and Chuseok holiday trains can have their own reservation schedule and rules — for Chuseok 2026, Korail ran a separate booking period that required membership, then opened remaining seats later, when non-members could buy and pay straight away. Check Korail's latest holiday notice if you're travelling around those dates.

> **Our take:** For Friday-to-Sunday trips, book as soon as your normal booking window opens. Those are also the days with higher cancellation fees, so pick your train with care.

Source: [Korail — ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets) and [2026 Chuseok reservations notice](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/siteInfo/notice/25622); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Buying at the station

![Korail ticket counters, ticket machines and departure boards at Pyeongtaek Station](/img/photo-korail-ticket-counter.jpg?v=00f643af "Korail ticket counters and machines at Pyeongtaek Station, 2024. Photo: MNXANL (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

You can also buy at ticket machines or the counter in a train station. Note that this means a railway station — Korail says KTX tickets aren't sold at subway stations.

Source: [Korail — ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## If your plans change

Before departure, you can cancel online — in MY TICKET for tickets booked on Korail's English website. After the train has left, the English guide directs you to a station counter. Korail's Korean guide also lists an exception: KTX tickets bought through KORAIL+ can be refunded in the app up to 10 minutes after departure, if it's confirmed that you're not on the train. Follow the refund options for the channel you bought from. Refunds aren't possible after the arrival time printed on the ticket.

The fee depends on when you cancel and on the day of travel. "The day before" means the previous calendar date, not a rolling 24-hour period:

| When you cancel | Mon–Thu trains (excluding public holidays and designated holiday periods) | Fri–Sun, public holidays, Seollal and Chuseok |
|---|---|---|
| From booking until 2 days before departure | No fee | Minimum fee |
| The day before departure | No fee | 5% |
| On the departure date, until 3 hours before | No fee | 10% |
| Less than 3 hours before departure | 5% | 20% |
| Up to 20 minutes after departure | 15% | 30% |
| 20 to 60 minutes after departure | 40% | 40% |
| 60 minutes after departure until arrival | 70% | 70% |

Korail's Korean guide lists the minimum fee as ₩400.

Source: [Korail — purchase and refund guide](https://www.korail.com/ticket/reserve/guide/pay) (Korean) and [ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Is the KORAIL PASS worth it?

The KORAIL PASS is a rail pass for foreign visitors. The current select passes let you choose 2, 3, 4 or 5 travel days within a 10-day period from the pass's starting date:

| Pass | Adult (13+) | Child (6–12) |
|---|---|---|
| 2-day select | ₩131,000 | ₩66,000 |
| 3-day select | ₩186,000 | ₩93,000 |
| 4-day select | ₩234,000 | ₩117,000 |
| 5-day select | ₩275,000 | ₩138,000 |

You need a valid passport and a credit card to buy it, and the details must match your passport. Choose your travel dates in MY TICKET before reserving seats; seat reservations open two months before departure, up to two seat tickets per person per day. Board with your pass, your passport and, if you reserved one, your seat reservation. Refunds are possible only before the pass's starting date.

Korail's current pass guide lists metropolitan railways and temporary tourist trains as not included. An older notice from 2024 also excluded SRT trains, which have run as KTX since September 2026. If your plans use trains from Suseo Station, check that a seat reservation is available for that train when you book, or ask Korail's call center (+82-1599-7777).

Source: [Korail — About KORAIL PASS](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/korailpass), [pass reservation](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/korailpass/reservation) and [older pass notice](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/siteInfo/notice/18801); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Our take:** Do the sums for your own trip. A 2-day pass costs ₩131,000, while a Seoul–Busan return in standard class is ₩108,800 (₩54,400 each way via Gyeongju) — so for one return trip, regular tickets are cheaper. A pass can make sense when you're fitting several long trips into a short window.

## Before you travel

1. Decide your stations — trains to Busan leave from Seoul Station and Suseo Station, among others.
2. Book from 07:00 (Korea time) two months ahead for weekend trips — and check Korail's holiday notice if you're travelling around Seollal or Chuseok.
3. Save your booking email and password.
4. Check you'll have data on the day for the app or your ticket — see [eSIM vs SIM card vs pocket Wi-Fi](/esim-sim-card-pocket-wifi-korea/).
5. Plan the trip to the station: [how to use Naver Map](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/) and [how to get a T-money card](/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/).

## FAQ

### Can foreigners book KTX tickets online?

Yes. Korail runs an English site for foreigners at korail.com/global/eng, and tickets can also be bought in the KORAIL+ app, at ticket machines and at station counters.

### How far in advance can I book the KTX?

Korail's normal booking window opens at 07:00 (Korea time), two months before the departure date. Seollal and Chuseok holiday trains can follow a separate schedule.

### How much is the KTX from Seoul to Busan?

₩54,400 for an adult in standard class from Seoul Station via Gyeongju, and ₩52,900 from Suseo Station, according to Korail's fare table effective September 1, 2026. Other routes between the two cities can cost a different amount.

### Is the SRT still separate from the KTX?

No. The government says the KTX and SRT started running as one KTX service on September 1, 2026, with integrated trains booked through KORAIL+ and the Korail website.

### Can I get a refund on a KTX ticket?

Yes. Before departure you can cancel online; after departure, generally at a station counter (KORAIL+ KTX tickets can be refunded in the app up to 10 minutes after departure if you're not on the train). No refunds after arrival. Fees depend on timing and the day of travel. For non-holiday Monday–Thursday departures, cancellation more than three hours before departure is free. Public holidays and the designated Seollal/Chuseok travel periods use the holiday fee schedule.

## Sources

# K-ETA Explained: Do You Need One to Visit Korea?

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/k-eta-korea/
Last checked: 2026-10-23

## Quick answer

- K-ETA is an online travel authorization for people who can enter Korea without a visa. Where it's required, you need approval before you board your flight or ship.
- 22 countries and regions are temporarily exempt until December 31, 2026 (Korea time), including the US, Canada, the UK, Japan and Australia. Check the official list, then confirm on the K-ETA site.
- Apply only on the official site (k-eta.go.kr) or the K-ETA app. The fee is ₩10,000 (about US$7–8, plus a separate online payment fee), and approval usually takes up to 72 hours.

If you can visit Korea without a visa, you've probably seen the letters K-ETA and wondered whether they apply to you. Short answer: maybe not right now. Korea runs the K-ETA system, but some countries and regions are temporarily exempt until the end of 2026 — and the official site is the place to check which side of that line you're on.

![Graphic: K-ETA in brief — who it's for, the temporary exemption until December 31, 2026, the fee and processing time](/img/keta-facts.png?v=0f511aef "K-ETA at a glance. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| | What the official site says |
|---|---|
| Who it's for | People who can enter Korea without a visa, visiting short-term for travel, family, events or business (no commercial activities) |
| When you need it | Before you board your flight or ship to Korea |
| Temporary exemption | 22 countries and regions don't need it until December 31, 2026 (KST) |
| Fee | ₩10,000 (about US$7–8), plus a separate online payment fee — not refunded if refused |
| Processing time | Typically 72 hours or less; no paid fast track |
| Valid for | 3 years, or until your passport expires if that's sooner |
| Where to apply | k-eta.go.kr or the official K-ETA app |

Source: [K-ETA — application guide](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaapplication.do), [eligible countries](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaalification.do) and [exemption notice](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/board/viewboarddetail.do?bbsSn=299707&esntlPnotiMtYn=Y); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## What K-ETA is (and isn't)

K-ETA is Korea's Electronic Travel Authorization. It's for travelers from countries and regions whose citizens can enter Korea without a visa. Where it applies, you need approval before you board your flight or ship — the official guide warns that applying after boarding, or once you're already in Korea, can lead to refusal or entry restrictions.

It isn't a visa. The site is clear that an approved K-ETA doesn't guarantee entry: the final decision is made by an immigration officer when you arrive. And it doesn't change how long you can stay. The K-ETA validity is separate from your visa-free stay — for example, the official list shows 90 days for US citizens and 6 months for Canadians.

Source: [K-ETA — application guide](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaapplication.do) and [eligible countries](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaalification.do); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## The temporary exemption, until December 31, 2026

Korea's Ministry of Justice has extended a temporary K-ETA exemption for one more year: it runs from January 1 to December 31, 2026 (Korea time) and applies to the countries and regions that were already exempt.

The extension notice itself doesn't list the countries, but the Korea Tourism Organization publishes the list of 22 countries and regions covered through December 31, 2026:

- **Asia:** Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, Macau
- **North America:** United States (including Guam), Canada
- **Europe:** United Kingdom, Germany, France, Italy, Netherlands, Spain, Poland, Sweden, Finland, Norway, Belgium, Denmark, Austria
- **Oceania:** Australia, New Zealand

Check that official list, and confirm your own status on the K-ETA site before you travel: if you're exempt, you'll see a pop-up message when you scan the photo page of your passport during the application.

Even if you're exempt, you can still choose to apply — the notice mentions benefits such as not having to fill in an arrival card. In that case you pay the fee, and it isn't refunded. The temporary K-ETA exemption alone does not exempt you from the arrival card. If you travel without a valid K-ETA, [check whether you need to submit an e-Arrival Card](https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/guide/eacTargetGuide.do); other exemptions, such as holding a valid Korean Residence Card, may apply. The official service is free.

Source: [K-ETA — notice on extension of temporary exemption](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/board/viewboarddetail.do?bbsSn=299707&esntlPnotiMtYn=Y) (posted Dec 23, 2025), [Korea Tourism Organization — visa & travel requirements](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140769) (updated Sep 18, 2026) and [e-Arrival Card — who needs to submit](https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/guide/eacTargetGuide.do); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Our take:** If you'll be entering Korea in 2027, check the latest official notice before you travel. The extension notice cited here confirms the temporary exemption only through December 31, 2026 (KST).

## Who doesn't need to apply

The official FAQ lists people who are exempt from applying, including:

- Holders of a valid Korean passport (including dual nationals)
- Registered foreigners and people with a Korean visa
- Children aged 17 and under, and adults aged 65 and over, on the date of entry
- Transfer passengers — unless you need to enter Korea because of an itinerary change or to collect your baggage
- Cruise travelers
- Flight attendants and seafarers, ABTC (APEC) card holders, UN passport holders, diplomatic and official passport holders, and active-duty US service members under the US–Korea SOFA

Source: [K-ETA — FAQ, "Who is eligible for the application exemption?"](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/board/viewboardlist.do?tmpltNm=faq2); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## How to apply

![The arrivals hall of Incheon Airport Terminal 1, seen from the floor above](/img/photo-icn-t1-arrivals.jpg?v=66c8964f "Incheon Airport Terminal 1 arrivals hall, 2023. Photo: ノボホショコロトソ (CC BY 4.0), cropped.")

Have these ready: a valid passport, an email address you can check, an ID photo, and a credit or debit card for the fee. Then:

1. Go to **k-eta.go.kr** (or the official K-ETA app) and choose to apply as a member or a non-member.
2. Enter your passport details — this is the point where exempt travelers see the pop-up.
3. Enter your travel details, check everything, and pay the ₩10,000 fee.
4. Wait for the result. The site says it typically takes 72 hours or less, but it can take longer when applications spike, and there's no expedited service.

Source: [K-ETA — official website](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/newapply/index.do?locale=EN), [application guide](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaapplication.do) and [what to prepare](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaalification.do); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Apply well before your flight rather than counting on the 72-hour figure, and make sure the details you enter match your passport exactly. The site warns that false or inaccurate information can get an approval refused or cancelled.

## Watch out for fake K-ETA sites

The official site carries a warning about look-alike agencies and phishing sites that charge high fees for "agency" or "expedited" K-ETA applications. The site says applications are accepted only at www.k-eta.go.kr or through the K-ETA mobile app, and it offers no paid fast track.

Source: [K-ETA — official website](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/newapply/index.do?locale=EN) and [application guide](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaapplication.do); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## After you're approved

- **Use it again.** A K-ETA can be used for multiple trips during its 3-year validity (or until your passport expires, if sooner).
- **Skip the arrival card — when you enter on your K-ETA.** If you also hold a Korean visa and enter on that visa, the official [e-Arrival Card guide](https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/guide/eacTargetGuide.do) says you must complete an e-Arrival Card.
- **New passport, new K-ETA.** If your passport is reissued — or your criminal record or infectious disease information changes — you need to apply again.
- **Keep your travel details up to date.** If your purpose of visit, address in Korea, contact details, travel dates or companions change, update them on the official site.

Source: [K-ETA — application guide](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaapplication.do) and [e-Arrival Card — who needs to submit](https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/guide/eacTargetGuide.do); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Before you fly

1. Check the [official exempt list](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140769), then confirm on k-eta.go.kr — scan your passport and see if the exemption pop-up appears.
2. Using the temporary exemption without a valid K-ETA? [Check whether you need to submit the free e-Arrival Card](https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/guide/eacTargetGuide.do), unless another arrival-card exemption applies.
3. If you need a K-ETA, apply on the official site or app and pay ₩10,000.
4. Allow time for processing before your flight.
5. Plan your arrival: [Incheon Airport to Seoul](/incheon-airport-to-seoul/), [getting online](/esim-sim-card-pocket-wifi-korea/) and [paying in Korea](/paying-in-korea-foreign-cards-cash/).

Source: [K-ETA — official website](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/newapply/index.do?locale=EN) and [exemption notice](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/board/viewboarddetail.do?bbsSn=299707&esntlPnotiMtYn=Y); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## FAQ

### Do I need a K-ETA to visit Korea in 2026?

It depends on your passport. K-ETA is for people who can enter Korea without a visa, but 22 countries and regions — including the US, Canada, the UK, Japan and Australia — are temporarily exempt until December 31, 2026 (KST). The K-ETA site shows a pop-up if you're exempt when you scan your passport.

### How much does a K-ETA cost?

₩10,000 (about US$7–8), plus a separate online payment fee. It isn't refunded if your application is refused.

### How long does K-ETA approval take?

The official site says typically 72 hours or less, though it can take longer. There's no expedited service.

### How long is a K-ETA valid?

3 years, or until your passport expires if that's sooner. You can use it for multiple trips, but each stay is still limited to your visa-free period.

### Do children need a K-ETA?

Children aged 17 and under on the date of entry are on the official list of people exempt from applying, as are adults aged 65 and over.

## Sources

- K-ETA (Ministry of Justice) — official website: https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/newapply/index.do?locale=EN
- K-ETA — Application guide (fee, processing time, validity): https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaapplication.do
- K-ETA — Eligible countries and what to prepare: https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaalification.do
- K-ETA — Notice on extension of K-ETA temporary exemption (Dec 23, 2025): https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/board/viewboarddetail.do?bbsSn=299707&esntlPnotiMtYn=Y
- K-ETA — FAQ (who is exempt from applying): https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/board/viewboardlist.do?tmpltNm=faq2
- Korea Tourism Organization — Visa & travel requirements (K-ETA exempt countries and regions): https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140769
- e-Arrival Card (Ministry of Justice) — who needs to submit: https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/guide/eacTargetGuide.do

# Korea First-Timer Checklist: What to Sort Before You Fly

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/korea-first-time-checklist/
Last checked: 2026-10-23

## Quick answer

- Check your entry permission first. Visa-free visitors normally need a K-ETA, but 22 countries and regions are temporarily exempt until December 31, 2026 (Korea time).
- Then see whether you need an e-Arrival Card. It's free and can be submitted within 3 days before you arrive; the official site has a quick checker.
- Pack for 220-volt sockets with two round holes, and declare food or more than US$10,000 in cash at customs.

Small practical problems can trip up a first trip to Korea: a phone with no data at the arrivals gate, a charger that won't fit the wall, a top-up machine that only takes cash. None of it is hard to fix once you're there, but it's easier to sort at home. This list runs roughly in the order you'll need things, from before you book your flight to your first night in Korea.

![Graphic: Korea first-timer checklist — entry, arrival card, packing, phone and money, emergency numbers](/img/checklist-steps.png?v=b7365dff "The checklist at a glance. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| When | What to sort |
|---|---|
| Before you book | Visa, K-ETA, or the temporary K-ETA exemption |
| 3 days before you land | The e-Arrival Card, if you need one (free) |
| A week before you land | Q-CODE or a health questionnaire, if your recent travel requires it |
| When you pack | An adapter for 220-volt, two-round-hole sockets; nothing you'd have to declare by accident |
| Before you leave home | Phone data, a card that works abroad, some won, and your route from the airport |
| Save in your phone | 112, 119 and 1330 |

Source: [e-Arrival Card](https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/main/index.do?locale=EN), [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140769) and [Korea Customs Service](https://www.customs.go.kr/english/cm/cntnts/cntntsView.do?mi=8069&cntntsId=2743); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## 1. Entry permission: visa, K-ETA or neither

Start here, because it decides everything else. If your passport lets you enter Korea without a visa, you normally need a K-ETA (an online travel authorization) before you board. Right now, though, 22 countries and regions are temporarily exempt until December 31, 2026 (Korea time), including the US, Canada, the UK, Japan and Australia. Visa-free travelers who are not covered by a K-ETA exemption need approval before boarding. Check both your nationality and personal exemptions, including those for travelers aged 17 or under and 65 or over on the date of entry. If you are not eligible for visa-free entry, check the visa requirements for your trip.

Our [K-ETA guide](/k-eta-korea/) has the full exempt list, the fee and how to avoid fake application sites.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — visa & travel requirements](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140769) (updated Sep 18, 2026) and [K-ETA FAQ](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/board/viewboardlist.do?tmpltNm=faq2); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## 2. The e-Arrival Card

This is the one people forget. Korea's arrival card is now an online form, and whether you need it depends on what you're entering with — not just your nationality. Travelers entering on a Korean visa need one, and so do travelers using the temporary K-ETA exemption, unless another exemption applies (a valid Korean residence card, for example). If you enter on a valid K-ETA, you don't. And if you hold both a K-ETA and a visa but enter on the visa, you do.

If that sounds like a puzzle, the official site has a checker: tick what you'll hold on arrival (visa, K-ETA, residence card or none) and it tells you. The service is free, and you can submit within 3 days before you arrive. Have your passport, your flight details and where you're staying ready, plus an email address.

Source: [e-Arrival Card — official site](https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/main/index.do?locale=EN) and [who needs to submit](https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/guide/eacTargetGuide.do); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Use the official site, e-arrivalcard.go.kr, and nothing that asks for a fee. Its notice board has also posted about delayed emails to Gmail and QQ.com addresses, so if a confirmation doesn't arrive, check that notice before you resubmit.

## 3. Q-CODE, if it applies to you

Q-CODE is Korea's online quarantine declaration. Whether you need to declare depends on where you stayed or transited. Korea's disease control agency (KDCA) splits this in two: all travelers who stayed in or transited through an intensive quarantine management area must declare, while for other quarantine management areas the requirement applies to travelers with relevant symptoms. If you need to declare, you can register in Q-CODE in advance or submit a Health Questionnaire. Q-CODE registration opens seven days before you arrive; if you finish it before boarding, you just show the QR code at quarantine screening.

The lists of areas change, so check KDCA's current guidance for the places on your route rather than relying on an old forum post.

Source: [KDCA — quarantine guide](https://travelhealth.kdca.go.kr/travel/www/QRNTN_INFO/QRNTN_INFO_MAIN.jsp) (Korean) and [Korea Tourism Organization — visa & travel requirements](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140769); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## 4. Packing: plugs and customs

![A white double wall socket with two round holes](/img/photo-korea-wall-socket.jpg?v=d8e4e758 "A double wall socket with two round holes. Photo: Melsj (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

Korean sockets have two round holes, and the standard supply is 220 volts at 60 hertz. If your plugs have flat pins, pack an adapter. Forgot one? The Korea Tourism Organization says you can ask your hotel's front desk to lend or sell you one, and you'll also find them at the airport, duty-free shops and convenience stores.

Customs is mostly about two things visitors carry without thinking. Food is one: meat, fruit, vegetables and other food products are on the list of goods to declare. But declaring something doesn't make it allowed in. Some products are banned outright (the Korea Tourism Organization's quarantine guide lists all fresh fruits and vegetables, for example), and animal products need a quarantine certificate from the exporting country and an inspection on arrival. Check the official animal and plant quarantine rules before you pack, and declare anything you're unsure about. Cash is the other: more than US$10,000 in cash or other means of payment has to be declared. The duty-free allowance for goods is US$800 in total, with separate rules for alcohol, tobacco and perfume.

If you take prescription medicine, check the customs guide first: some medicines are on the declaration list.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — electricity & communications](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140041) (updated Sep 11, 2026) and [animal and plant quarantine](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140629) (updated Sep 28, 2026), and [Korea Customs Service — customs clearance guide for passengers](https://www.customs.go.kr/english/cm/cntnts/cntntsView.do?mi=8069&cntntsId=2743); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Look at the input rating printed on each charger before you go. An adapter only changes the shape of the plug, not the voltage.

## 5. Phone, data and maps

You'll want data from the moment you leave the plane: to find the train, to message your hotel, and to walk the last few hundred meters from a subway exit. Decide before you fly whether you'll use an eSIM, a Korean SIM card or a pocket Wi-Fi router. Our [eSIM, SIM card and pocket Wi-Fi guide](/esim-sim-card-pocket-wifi-korea/) compares them.

Install your map app at home, too. When we tested the Google Maps website on a Seoul route (Oct 22, 2026), it gave transit directions but no walking or driving routes, which is why our [Naver Map guide](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/) exists.

## 6. Money and the transit card

A foreign card works in most hotels, shops and taxis, but not everywhere — and topping up a regular T-money transit card takes Korean won cash. Bring a card that works abroad and plan to get some won early. Our guides cover [paying in Korea](/paying-in-korea-foreign-cards-cash/) and [getting a T-money card](/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/).

## 7. Your first ride and your longer trips

![Travelers collecting luggage at the baggage claim in Incheon Airport Terminal 2](/img/photo-icn-t2-baggage-claim.jpg?v=6748e64b "Baggage claim, Incheon Airport Terminal 2, 2024. Photo: AirportTerminalGuy (CC BY 4.0), cropped.")

Know how you'll get from the airport before you're standing at baggage claim with a dead phone. Our [Incheon Airport to Seoul guide](/incheon-airport-to-seoul/) compares the airport railroad, buses and taxis.

If you're planning Busan, Gyeongju or another city by KTX, note when tickets go on sale: the normal booking window opens two months ahead, and holiday trains follow their own schedule. [How to book KTX tickets](/how-to-book-ktx-korea/) walks through it.

## 8. Numbers to save before you go

In an emergency, call 112 for the police or 119 for fire and ambulance. If you don't speak Korean, say "English please" or "Interpreter please" when the call connects, and an interpreter will be brought in. The government's Baro Emergency Reporting App is another way to report.

For anything that isn't an emergency (lost, confused, a problem with a shop or taxi), the Korea Travel Helpline is 1330 from a Korean phone, or +82-2-1330 from overseas. It also runs a real-time chat, and its online voice call is free over Wi-Fi.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — disaster safety services](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=248145) and [1330 Travel Helpline](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140632); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Our take:** Save 1330 under a name you'll recognize. Besides travel information, it handles interpretation and tourist complaints.

## The checklist

1. Check whether you need a visa, a K-ETA, or neither — [K-ETA guide](/k-eta-korea/).
2. Run the e-Arrival Card checker; if you need one, submit it within 3 days before you land.
3. Check KDCA's current quarantine areas and symptom rules; submit Q-CODE or a Health Questionnaire if required.
4. Pack an adapter for two-round-hole sockets; check your chargers' voltage.
5. Check the quarantine rules before packing food (fresh fruit and vegetables are banned); declare food and cash over US$10,000.
6. Sort phone data — [eSIM, SIM or pocket Wi-Fi](/esim-sim-card-pocket-wifi-korea/).
7. Install [Naver Map](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/).
8. Bring a card that works abroad and plan for some won — [paying in Korea](/paying-in-korea-foreign-cards-cash/).
9. Plan your [airport route](/incheon-airport-to-seoul/) and any [KTX trips](/how-to-book-ktx-korea/).
10. Save 112, 119 and 1330 in your phone.

## FAQ

### Do I need an arrival card for Korea?

It depends on what you enter with. Travelers entering on a Korean visa, and travelers using the temporary K-ETA exemption, generally need the e-Arrival Card; travelers entering on a valid K-ETA don't. Some other exemptions, such as a valid Korean residence card, also apply. The official e-Arrival Card site has a free checker.

### When can I submit the e-Arrival Card?

The official site says to complete and submit it within 3 days before you arrive in Korea. There's no fee.

### What plug does Korea use?

Korean sockets have two round holes, and the supply is 220 volts at 60 hertz, according to the Korea Tourism Organization.

### Can I bring food into Korea?

Food products, including meat, fruit and vegetables, are on Korea Customs Service's list of goods you must declare, but declaring them doesn't make them admissible. Some, such as all fresh fruits and vegetables, are banned, and animal products need a quarantine certificate from the exporting country and an inspection. Check the official quarantine rules before packing.

### What number do I call for help in Korea?

112 for police and 119 for fire and ambulance in an emergency. For travel help, call the Korea Travel Helpline on 1330 in Korea or +82-2-1330 from overseas.

## Sources

- Korea Tourism Organization — Visa & travel requirements (K-ETA, Q-Code): https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140769
- Korea Tourism Organization — Electricity & communications: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140041

# Tax Refund in Korea: How Visitors Get Money Back on Shopping

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/korea-tax-refund-guide/
Last checked: 2026-10-23

## Quick answer

- Foreign visitors staying in Korea for less than 6 months can claim back VAT on goods bought at stores that show a Tax Refund sign, for purchases of ₩15,000 or more in a single transaction.
- Instant refunds at the till work for purchases under ₩1,000,000 each, up to ₩5,000,000 in total per trip — just show your passport.
- For other refunds, finish export clearance before you send your bags off: scan your passport at the airport refund kiosk, and if it asks for a customs inspection, show the unopened goods. No customs confirmation, no refund.

Prices in Korean shops include value-added tax, and as a visitor you can get part of it back. The rules aren't complicated, but the one step people miss, getting their purchases cleared for export at the airport before they check their bags, is the one that costs them the refund. Here's how it works, from the till to the departure gate.

![Graphic: Korea tax refund at a glance — who qualifies, the ₩15,000 minimum, instant refund limits and the customs step](/img/taxrefund-steps.png?v=756d2ac5 "Tax refund in Korea at a glance. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| | What the rules say |
|---|---|
| Who | Foreign visitors staying in Korea for less than 6 months (and some overseas Koreans) |
| Where | Stores showing a "Tax Refund" sign with a refund company's logo |
| Minimum | ₩15,000 in a single transaction |
| Instant refund in store | Under ₩1,000,000 per purchase, up to ₩5,000,000 in total after you arrive |
| Take it out of Korea | Within 3 months of buying |
| How much back | Roughly 5–8% of the price, after fees |

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — comprehensive tax refund guide](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=248765) and the [Presidential Decree](https://www.law.go.kr/법령/외국인관광객등에대한부가가치세및개별소비세특례규정) and [enforcement rules](https://www.law.go.kr/법령/외국인관광객등에대한부가가치세및개별소비세특례규정시행규칙) in force from Jan 2, 2026 (Korean); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Who can claim

Foreign visitors staying in Korea for less than 6 months generally qualify, as do overseas Koreans who have lived abroad for at least 2 years and are staying in Korea for 3 months or less. You can't claim if you're staying 6 months or longer, work in Korea, or are a diplomat or US military personnel stationed in Korea. Purchases made under a company name or through someone else don't count either.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — comprehensive tax refund guide](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=248765); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## What you can claim on

Most goods qualify: clothes, shoes, bags, cosmetics, perfume, electronics, ginseng. A few things don't. Cooked food and services such as massages are out, because customs can't inspect them when you leave. So are items you've opened or used before taking them out of Korea, anything bought duty-free, and goods that are banned anyway.

Two practical rules matter more than the list. First, only stores that offer tax refunds count, and they show a "Tax Refund" sign with the refund company's logo. Second, an ordinary receipt isn't enough: ask for the tax refund documents when you pay, and keep them until you leave.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — comprehensive tax refund guide](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=248765); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Keep tax-free purchases sealed until you're home. Items opened or used before you take them out of Korea aren't eligible, so leave the packaging sealed.

## Instant refund: the easy way

At stores that offer it, you show your passport and pay the price with the tax already taken off. In the official guide, the steps for an instant refund end there: check eligibility with your passport, pay the lower price, then leave Korea as normal. The limits are set in law: each purchase must be under ₩1,000,000, and your instant-refund purchases since arriving can't exceed ₩5,000,000 in total. The store can deduct an approved processing fee from the tax amount.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — comprehensive tax refund guide](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=248765) and the [Presidential Decree](https://www.law.go.kr/법령/외국인관광객등에대한부가가치세및개별소비세특례규정) (Korean); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## General refund: pay now, claim later

Everything else works the other way round. You pay the full price, take the refund voucher, and claim the money later in one of four ways:

- **Downtown:** at a staffed refund center or an unmanned kiosk in the city, for single purchases of ₩6,000,000 or less. Bring your passport, the voucher and a credit card. You still have to get the customs check when you leave.
- **At the airport:** through the refund kiosk and, if needed, the customs check, then at a refund counter or kiosk.
- **By mailbox:** at ports without a refund counter, drop the customs-confirmed voucher in the mailbox, with your details and refund method written on it.
- **By mobile:** submit the customs-confirmed voucher through the refund company's app or website.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — comprehensive tax refund guide](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=248765); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## At the airport: the order that matters

![The departure hall of Incheon Airport Terminal 2, with self bag-drop machines and check-in counters](/img/photo-icn-t2-departures.jpg?v=e4143de1 "Departure hall, Incheon Airport Terminal 2, 2024. Photo: AirportTerminalGuy (CC BY 4.0), cropped.")

For general refunds, the goods need export clearance before they leave with you, and customs may ask to inspect them. Incheon Airport describes the order like this:

1. Check in. The airport advises carrying refund-eligible items and their documents with you rather than checking them.
2. If they are in a checked bag, tell the airline staff at check-in. The bag is tagged for customs inspection and you take it back.
3. Scan your passport at the refund kiosk in the departure hall. If the kiosk says your items need a customs inspection, show your passport, the unopened and unused goods and the purchase confirmation at the customs desk.
4. A checked bag that customs has cleared goes onto the oversized baggage belt next to the customs desk.
5. After security and immigration, collect the refund at the refund counter or kiosk in the duty-free area, or use the mailbox or mobile option.

Customs confirmation is described as an essential requirement: without it, there's no refund. If you miss it, the Korea Tourism Organization says you can still claim on a later trip, if you bring the goods and the voucher back within the voucher's validity period and get the customs check when you leave Korea again.

Incheon Airport lists these refund counters, both in the 3rd-floor duty-free area (after security and immigration):

| | Refund counter | Counter hours | Refund kiosk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Terminal 1 | Near Gate 28 | 07:00–22:00 | 24 hours, near Gate 28 |
| Terminal 2 | Near Gate 253, across from Gate 250 | 07:00–21:30 | 24 hours, same area |

The airport says its information is for reference only, so allow extra time and follow the signs on the day.

Source: [Incheon International Airport — domestic tax refund](https://www.airport.kr/ap_en/1425/subview.do) and [Korea Tourism Organization — comprehensive tax refund guide](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=248765) (FAQ); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## How much you actually get back

Don't expect the full 10% VAT. The Korea Tourism Organization puts the refund at roughly 5–8% of the purchase price after the refund company's processing fee, depending on the price, the company and how you're paid. Taking the refund on a credit card or by mobile payment adds a separate fee, so taking cash at the counter avoids that extra fee. On a ₩100,000 purchase, 5–8% works out to about ₩5,000–₩8,000.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — comprehensive tax refund guide](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=248765) (FAQ); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Our take:** Where a store offers it, the instant refund is usually simpler, because the tax comes off when you pay. Check the net price and any processing fee, keep your purchase records, take the goods out within the required period, and follow any customs instructions. Use the general refund when an instant refund isn't available or a purchase is over the limits.

## Duty-free or tax refund?

They're different systems. Duty-free shops at airports and in the city sell goods without customs duty or consumption taxes. Tax refund stores sell at normal prices and give back the VAT and individual consumption tax afterwards. For general refunds there's no overall spending limit, just the ₩15,000 minimum per purchase; instant refunds have the limits above. Either way, when you take purchases to another country, that country's import and duty-free rules apply. Korea's US$800 traveler allowance is for goods brought into Korea, not a universal allowance for taking purchases home.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — comprehensive tax refund guide](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=248765) (FAQ) and [Korea Customs Service — customs clearance guide for passengers](https://www.customs.go.kr/english/cm/cntnts/cntntsView.do?mi=8069&cntntsId=2743); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Before you shop, and before you fly

1. Carry your passport when you shop.
2. Look for the "Tax Refund" sign, and spend ₩15,000 or more in one transaction.
3. Ask for the tax refund documents, not just a receipt.
4. Keep tax-free goods unopened and unused.
5. At the airport, finish the refund kiosk and any customs inspection before your goods leave your hands.
6. Take the goods out of Korea within 3 months of buying them.

For the rest of your trip planning, see our [first-timer checklist](/korea-first-time-checklist/) and [paying in Korea](/paying-in-korea-foreign-cards-cash/).

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — comprehensive tax refund guide](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=248765) and [Incheon International Airport — domestic tax refund](https://www.airport.kr/ap_en/1425/subview.do); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## FAQ

### What is the minimum purchase for a tax refund in Korea?

₩15,000 in a single transaction at a tax refund store. The amount is set in Korea's enforcement rules, in force from Jan 2, 2026.

### What are the limits for an instant tax refund?

Each purchase must be under ₩1,000,000, and your instant-refund purchases since arriving in Korea can total up to ₩5,000,000.

### Do I need to show my purchases at the airport?

For general refunds, keep the goods with you until export clearance is done. At Incheon you scan your passport at the refund kiosk; if it asks for a customs inspection, show your passport, the unopened goods and the purchase confirmation at the customs desk. For instant refunds, follow any customs instructions you are given.

### Can I get a tax refund with my receipt?

No. You need the tax refund documents that the store issues with your purchase.

### How much VAT do I get back in Korea?

About 5–8% of the purchase price after processing fees, according to the Korea Tourism Organization. A refund to a card or by mobile payment carries an extra fee.

## Sources

- Korea Tourism Organization — Comprehensive tax refund guide: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=248765
- Korean law — Special rules on VAT and individual consumption tax for foreign tourists (Presidential Decree, in force Jan 2, 2026; Korean): https://www.law.go.kr/법령/외국인관광객등에대한부가가치세및개별소비세특례규정
- Korean law — Enforcement rules of the special rules (in force Jan 2, 2026; Korean): https://www.law.go.kr/법령/외국인관광객등에대한부가가치세및개별소비세특례규정시행규칙
- Incheon International Airport — Domestic tax refund: https://www.airport.kr/ap_en/1425/subview.do
- Korea Customs Service — Customs clearance guide for passengers: https://www.customs.go.kr/english/cm/cntnts/cntntsView.do?mi=8069&cntntsId=2743

# Paying in Korea: Foreign Cards, Cash and What Still Needs Won

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/paying-in-korea-foreign-cards-cash/
Last checked: 2026-10-23

## Quick answer

- Credit cards are widely used — the Korea Tourism Organization names Visa, Mastercard and American Express — but check that each shop accepts your card, and carry some won for cash-only needs.
- Carry a little won anyway. A regular T-money card is topped up with Korean won cash.
- Landing at Incheon Terminal 1? The arrivals floor has currency exchange counters that are open 24 hours.

Cards are widely used in Korea. Hotels, department stores and most shops take them, and taxis accept card payment too — though no one can promise your particular card will work everywhere. The catch is the small stuff — a regular T-money top-up, the odd shop that doesn't take cards — and that's where a little Korean won saves you a walk to the ATM.

![Where a foreign card works in Korea: shops and hotels usually, taxis usually, new subway ticket machines yes with a fee, regular T-money top-ups at stores or stations need won cash](/img/pay-compare.png?v=96e100e5 "Card or cash? Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| Where | Foreign card? | Good to know |
|---|---|---|
| Hotels, department stores, most shops | Usually | Some stores don't take cards — check before you buy |
| Taxis | Usually — check before you get in | Cash, credit card or a transport card |
| Subway single tickets and Climate Card short-term passes | Yes, at the 440 new machines on Lines 1–8 | About 3.7% service fee |
| Topping up a regular T-money card at a store or station | No | Korean won cash |
| TABA taxi app | Yes | Visa, Mastercard, UnionPay, JCB |

Source: [VISITKOREA — currency](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140040) and [taxis](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140661); [Seoul Metropolitan Government](https://english.seoul.go.kr/climate-cards-and-single-journey-transit-tickets-now-accepting-international-credit-cards-no-cash-needed/); [T-money](https://pay.tmoney.co.kr/ncs/pct/ugd/ReadFrgnGd.dev); [TABA](https://www.tabataxi.app/); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Paying by card

The Korea Tourism Organization puts it simply: most businesses in Korea accept credit cards, from major hotels and department stores to general shops, and Visa, Mastercard and American Express can be used. It also adds a caution worth taking seriously — some stores don't provide card payment, so check before you buy.

Taxis are usually straightforward: VISITKOREA says passengers can pay with cash, a credit card or a transportation card. That's a general rule, not a promise that a particular foreign-issued card will go through, so it's worth checking as you get in.

Source: [VISITKOREA — Korean Currency & Exchange Info](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140040); [VISITKOREA — Taxis](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140661) (updated Jan 2026); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Where won still comes in handy

![Street-food stalls and shoppers on Myeongdong 7-gil in Seoul in the early evening](/img/photo-myeongdong-street-food.jpg?v=71464c29 "Myeongdong 7-gil, Seoul, 2023. Photo: SKTakek (CC0), cropped.")

The clearest case for cash is a regular T-money card topped up at a store or station. T-money's guide for visitors says you top it up by handing over the card and Korean won cash at a T-money sales location.

The subway itself has got easier. Since March 17, 2026, the 440 new ticket machines at 273 stations on Seoul Subway Lines 1–8 accept international cards such as Visa and Mastercard — for single-journey tickets and Climate Card short-term passes. Expect a service fee of about 3.7%. The former 30-day Climate Card pass is no longer available for top-up; the 1-, 2-, 3-, 5- and 7-day short-term passes continue to operate.

So if your plan is a T-money card, land with some won. If you'd rather carry as little cash as possible, the Climate Card short-term pass or single tickets are the card-friendly route on the subway.

Source: [T-money — guide for foreign visitors](https://pay.tmoney.co.kr/ncs/pct/ugd/ReadFrgnGd.dev); [Seoul Metropolitan Government](https://english.seoul.go.kr/climate-cards-and-single-journey-transit-tickets-now-accepting-international-credit-cards-no-cash-needed/) and [Seoul transport news](https://news.seoul.go.kr/traffic/archives/516544) (Korean), Mar 2026; and [Climate Card 30-day end-of-service FAQ](https://news.seoul.go.kr/traffic/public/climatecard-faq/faq-stop) (Korean); checked Oct 23, 2026. More on the card itself: [how to get a T-money card](/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/).

## Getting won when you land

VISITKOREA's advice is that for most tourists, the airport exchange centers are the easiest place to change money.

At Incheon Airport Terminal 1, the arrivals floor (1F) has:

- **24-hour exchange counters** — Woori Bank near Exits 6 and 11, and KB Bank near Arrival Hall B
- **Exchange counters open 06:00–22:00** — Hana Bank near Exit 4 and KB Bank near Exit 9
- **24-hour ATMs** near Exits 4, 6, 9 and 11

The airport's directory doesn't say which ATMs take foreign-issued cards, so look at the card logos on the machine before you put your card in. This list is for Terminal 1; check the airport's facility search if you arrive at Terminal 2.

In town, banks are generally open 09:00–16:00 on weekdays, and Korea Post Bank 09:00–16:30. Hours vary by branch, and some places won't exchange old banknotes.

Source: [VISITKOREA FAQ](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/faq/faqMainView.do?menuSn=404&pstSn=95); [Incheon Airport — Convenience & Public Facilities](https://www.airport.kr/ap_en/1536/subview.do); [VISITKOREA — currency](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140040); checked Oct 23, 2026. Getting into the city: [Incheon Airport to Seoul](/incheon-airport-to-seoul/).

> **Local tip:** Before you fly, check two things with your bank: that your card is set up for use abroad, and what it charges for foreign transactions and cash withdrawals. It's easier to sort out at home than at an ATM at midnight.

## Taxi apps and NAVER's visitor verification

**TABA** is a taxi app for travelers. Its official site says you can pay with Visa, Mastercard, China UnionPay, JCB and more, sign up with an international phone number, and that it works officially with the Seoul Metropolitan Government and T-money.

**NAVER** introduced Passport Verification on June 4, 2026, so eligible foreign visitors can verify their identity for supported booking and ordering services without a Korean mobile number. This is separate from payment approval. NAVER's Booking/Order help lists supported overseas card networks, while some Npay services are restricted to Npay Korea Members. Check the payment options shown for your booking before relying on a particular card. (If you're still choosing how to get online, see [eSIM vs SIM card vs pocket Wi-Fi](/esim-sim-card-pocket-wifi-korea/) — and [how to use Naver Map](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/).)

Source: [TABA](https://www.tabataxi.app/); [NAVER press release, Jun 9, 2026](https://www.navercorp.com/en/media/pressReleasesDetail?seq=10034413); NAVER Help — [passport verification](https://help.naver.com/service/5640/contents/25235?lang=ko&osType=COMMONOS), [supported cards](https://help.naver.com/service/11713/contents/24272?lang=en&osType=COMMONOS) and [Npay Korea Member restrictions](https://help.naver.com/service/11713/contents/24269?lang=en&osType=COMMONOS); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Prepaid travel cards

Some visitors use a prepaid card made for travelers. WOWPASS is one: its maker, Orange Square, describes it as an all-in-one prepaid card for foreign travelers covering money exchange, payment and transportation, and says you verify ownership in its app to withdraw a remaining balance in cash. Fees and limits change, so check the current terms in the app before you buy.

Source: [WOWPASS App Store listing (Orange Square, Inc)](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/wowpass-go-cashless-in-korea/id1626691440); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Our take

![Inside Gwangjang Market in Seoul: food stalls with Korean signs under strings of flags](/img/photo-gwangjang-market.jpg?v=aa69a454 "Gwangjang Market, Seoul, 2022. Photo: Bgag (CC0), cropped.")

> **Our take:** Plan to pay by card, but don't arrive with zero won. A small amount covers a T-money top-up and the occasional place that doesn't take cards, and it saves you hunting for an ATM at the wrong moment. If you'd rather skip cash on the subway, use the new ticket machines and accept the fee.

## Before you fly

1. Tell your bank you're travelling and check its foreign transaction and ATM fees.
2. Bring a backup card, kept separately from your main one.
3. Decide on your transit card — T-money (top up with won cash) or the Climate Card short-term pass (card-friendly at the new machines in Seoul).
4. Note where the 24-hour exchange counters are if you land late at Incheon Terminal 1.

## FAQ

### Can I use my foreign credit card in Korea?

Cards are widely used. The Korea Tourism Organization says Visa, Mastercard and American Express can be used, from hotels and department stores to general shops, but some stores don't take cards — check that each place accepts yours.

### Do I need cash in Korea?

A little. Topping up a regular T-money card at a store or station takes Korean won cash, and some shops don't accept cards.

### Can I buy Seoul subway tickets with a foreign card?

Yes, since March 17, 2026, at the 440 new ticket machines on Lines 1–8 — for single-journey tickets and Climate Card short-term passes, with a service fee of about 3.7%.

### Where can I exchange money at Incheon Airport?

Terminal 1's arrivals floor has 24-hour exchange counters (Woori Bank near Exits 6 and 11, KB Bank near Arrival Hall B), plus counters open 06:00–22:00 near Exits 4 and 9.

### Can I pay by card in a Korean taxi?

Usually. VISITKOREA says taxi passengers can pay with cash, a credit card or a transportation card — check that your card is accepted before you set off.

# Seoul Subway Guide for First-Timers: Fares, Tickets and Transfers

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/seoul-subway-guide/
Last checked: 2026-10-23

## Quick answer

- Standard adult fares start at ₩1,550 with a transit card (T-money) or ₩1,650 with a single-journey ticket for the first 10 km. Distance charges are ₩100 per 5 km up to 50 km, then ₩100 per 8 km; some lines add separate fares.
- Tap your card when you enter and when you leave. Skip the tap on the way out and you lose the transfer discount on your next bus or train.
- Single-journey tickets add a ₩500 deposit that you get back from a refund machine at your destination.

The Seoul subway is the easiest part of a first trip to Korea, once you know three things: what to pay with, that you tap out as well as in, and that a transfer to a bus can be discounted. Station signs include English, and the lines are numbered and color-coded. What catches visitors out is the fare system, so that's most of this guide.

![Graphic: Seoul subway in 4 steps — get a card or ticket, tap in, tap out, transfer if eligible](/img/subway-steps.png?v=ba9db5a8 "The Seoul subway in four steps. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| | Adult fare | Good to know |
|---|---|---|
| T-money (transit card) | ₩1,550 for the first 10 km | Top up with won cash; transfer discounts with buses |
| Single-journey ticket | ₩1,650 for the first 10 km | Plus a ₩500 deposit, refunded at your destination |
| Climate Card short-term pass | ₩5,000 (1 day) to ₩20,000 (7 days) | Unlimited rides in its coverage area; card costs ₩3,000 |
| Children aged 6–12 | ₩550 | T-money must be registered with the child's date of birth; under 6 free with a guardian (up to 3 children) |

Longer trips add ₩100 for every 5 km between 10 km and 50 km, and ₩100 for every 8 km after that. Some lines, such as the Sinbundang Line, add their own separate fare.

Source: [Seoul Metropolitan Government — subway fares](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/subway/) (as of Jun 28, 2025), [Seoul Metro — fare](http://www.seoulmetro.co.kr/en/page.do?menuIdx=348), [Sinbundang Line — fares](https://shinbundang.co.kr/dxline/dxline4_1.jsp) (Korean), [T-money — guide for foreigners](https://pay.tmoney.co.kr/ncs/pct/ugd/ReadFrgnGd.dev) and [Climate Card](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/climate-card/); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## What to pay with

For most visitors, a **T-money card** is the default. You pay the lower card fare, you get transfer discounts between subway and bus, and the same card works on buses. For a child to get the child fare, the card has to be registered with the child's date of birth first; T-money says this is done at convenience stores or subway information centers, with the card and an ID. An unregistered card charges the adult fare. The catch: regular T-money top-ups take Korean won cash. Our [T-money guide](/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/) covers where to buy one and how to get your balance back.

A **single-journey ticket** makes sense for one or two rides. It costs ₩100 more than the card fare, works only on the subway, and you pay a ₩500 deposit on top. To buy one, pick your language on the machine, choose "Single-Journey," then find your destination by station name or station number, and pay the fare plus deposit. At the end of your ride, after you tap out, put the ticket into the "Deposit Refund Device" at your destination station to get the ₩500 back before you leave the station.

The **Climate Card short-term pass** is Seoul's unlimited-ride option for 1, 2, 3, 5 or 7 days. The pass starts on the day you charge it, and a 1-day pass runs until that day's last bus or train. Since October 1, 2026, it covers subway stations within Seoul and Seoul-licensed city and village buses. You can also get off at Incheon Airport Terminal 1 or 2 on the Airport Railroad after boarding within the covered area, but you can't board with the pass at those airport stations. The Sinbundang Line and airport buses are excluded, and if you get off outside the coverage area, station staff will charge you the fare for that trip. Check the [official FAQ](https://news.seoul.go.kr/traffic/public/climatecard-faq/faq-short) (Korean) before you buy.

![A ticket vending and card reload machine with Korean and English labels on the Seoul Metropolitan Subway](/img/photo-seoul-subway-ticket-machine.jpg?v=432b2959 "A ticket vending and card reload machine, July 2024 (the fare on its screen predates the June 2025 fare change). Photo: LandAndTree (CC BY 4.0), cropped.")

Paying by foreign card? Since March 17, 2026, the 440 new ticket machines at 273 stations on Lines 1–8 accept international cards such as Visa and Mastercard for single-journey tickets and Climate Card short-term passes, with a service fee of about 3.7%.

Source: [Seoul Metro — single-journey ticket](http://www.seoulmetro.co.kr/en/page.do?menuIdx=719), [Seoul Metropolitan Government — Climate Card](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/climate-card/) and [international cards at ticket machines](https://english.seoul.go.kr/climate-cards-and-single-journey-transit-tickets-now-accepting-international-credit-cards-no-cash-needed/); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Our take:** Count your rides. A 1-day pass costs ₩5,000, and the basic T-money fare is ₩1,550, so the pass starts to pay off from your fourth separate basic-fare journey that day (transfers within one journey don't count as extra journeys), assuming you already have a Climate Card. If you'd be buying the card too, add ₩3,000 to the sum. For a couple of rides a day, plain T-money is simpler.

## Tap in, tap out

Tap your card on the reader at the gate when you go in, and again when you come out. Seoul Metro is direct about the cost of forgetting the second tap: if your card doesn't properly touch the reader when you get off, you lose the transfer discount and are charged separate fares for each ride. Climate Card short-term pass users should tap out too, though Seoul's current FAQ says missed-tap penalties don't apply to short-term passes.

There's one small reward for early starts: your first ride before 6:30 a.m. is 20% off when you pay by card.

Source: [Seoul Metro — fare](http://www.seoulmetro.co.kr/en/page.do?menuIdx=348), [Seoul Metropolitan Government — subway fares](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/subway/) and [Climate Card short-term FAQ](https://news.seoul.go.kr/traffic/public/climatecard-faq/faq-short) (Korean); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Transfers: how the discount works

On standard subway lines, changing lines within the paid area doesn't add a new base fare; the journey's distance still counts. Lines such as Sinbundang charge an additional line-specific fare. Switching between the subway and a bus is where the transfer rules matter. With a transit card, a journey can include up to four transfers, for five boardings in total. Tap on and off each time, and board the next bus or train within 30 minutes of getting off, or within 60 minutes between 9 p.m. and 7 a.m. You pay the highest base fare among the services you use, plus any distance or line surcharges, rather than a new fare each time. Transfers to the same bus route or the same vehicle don't count. Single-journey tickets don't get bus transfers, since they work only on the subway.

Source: [Seoul Metropolitan Government — integrated transfer discount](https://news.seoul.go.kr/traffic/transfer_discount) (Korean), [Seoul Metro — fare](http://www.seoulmetro.co.kr/en/page.do?menuIdx=348) and [Sinbundang Line — fares](https://shinbundang.co.kr/dxline/dxline4_1.jsp) (Korean); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Finding your way

![Seoul Station platform on Subway Line 4 with a yellow Way Out sign overhead](/img/photo-seoul-subway-platform.jpg?v=e8e0034c "Seoul Station, Subway Line 4, 2023. Photo: Mobius6 (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

Lines have numbers and colors, and stations have numbers as well as names, which helps when a station name is long or unfamiliar. Plan routes in [Naver Map](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/), which gives transit directions in English.

> **Local tip:** Before you leave the platform, check which exit number your map suggests. Big stations have many exits, and the right one can save you a long walk above ground. Late at night, check your last train in the app too, because last-train times differ by line and station.

## Before your first ride

1. Get a T-money card and some won to top it up — or plan to use a single ticket or a Climate Card pass.
2. Install Naver Map and search your first route.
3. Tap in at the gate. Tap out when you leave.
4. Using a single ticket? After tapping out, return it at the destination station's refund machine before leaving the station.
5. Heading on by bus? Board within 30 minutes (60 at night) to keep the transfer discount.

Source: [Seoul Metro — single-journey ticket](http://www.seoulmetro.co.kr/en/page.do?menuIdx=719) and [Seoul Metropolitan Government — integrated transfer discount](https://news.seoul.go.kr/traffic/transfer_discount) (Korean); checked Oct 23, 2026.

Arriving from the airport? See [Incheon Airport to Seoul](/incheon-airport-to-seoul/). Heading farther? See [how to book KTX tickets](/how-to-book-ktx-korea/).

## FAQ

### How much is the Seoul subway?

₩1,550 for adults with a transit card such as T-money, or ₩1,650 with a single-journey ticket, for up to 10 km on standard lines. Longer trips add ₩100 per 5 km up to 50 km, then ₩100 per 8 km. Some lines, such as Sinbundang, add a separate fare.

### Can I use a credit card to ride the Seoul subway?

At the gates you tap a transit card or ticket. To buy one by card: since March 17, 2026, the 440 new machines on Lines 1–8 sell single-journey tickets and Climate Card short-term passes to holders of international cards such as Visa and Mastercard, with a fee of about 3.7%.

### Do I get my single-ticket deposit back?

Yes. The ₩500 deposit is refunded in full when you put the ticket into the Deposit Refund Device at your destination station.

### Are transfers free on the Seoul subway?

On standard lines, changing lines inside the paid area doesn't add a new base fare. Between subway and bus, a transit card gives a transfer discount if you tap on and off and board within 30 minutes (60 minutes between 9 p.m. and 7 a.m.), up to four transfers (five boardings). You pay the highest base fare among the services used, plus distance and line surcharges; transfers to the same bus route don't count.

### Do children pay on the Seoul subway?

Children aged 6–12 pay ₩550 for the basic fare, but with T-money the card must first be registered with the child's date of birth, or it charges the adult fare. Children under 6 ride free with a guardian, up to three children per guardian.

## Sources

- Seoul Metropolitan Government — Subway fares: https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/subway/
- Seoul Metro — Fare: http://www.seoulmetro.co.kr/en/page.do?menuIdx=348
- Seoul Metro — Single-journey ticket: http://www.seoulmetro.co.kr/en/page.do?menuIdx=719
- Seoul Metropolitan Government — Climate Card: https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/climate-card/
- Seoul Climate Card FAQ, short-term passes (Korean): https://news.seoul.go.kr/traffic/public/climatecard-faq/faq-short
- Seoul Metropolitan Government — Integrated transfer discount (Korean): https://news.seoul.go.kr/traffic/transfer_discount
- T-money — Guide for foreigners: https://pay.tmoney.co.kr/ncs/pct/ugd/ReadFrgnGd.dev
- Sinbundang Line — Fares (Korean): https://shinbundang.co.kr/dxline/dxline4_1.jsp
- Seoul Metropolitan Government — International cards for passes and single tickets (Mar 2026): https://english.seoul.go.kr/climate-cards-and-single-journey-transit-tickets-now-accepting-international-credit-cards-no-cash-needed/
